findings.scenario: The moving streamer reaches the obstruction before the viewer counter resolves.
findings.gap: The proposed loop has no defined actionable decision, activation order, collision consequence or movement policy outside planning.
findings.recommendation: Specify a paper timeline connecting readable warning, streamer choice, counter eligibility, activation and recovery. Have the user select controls and consequences; preserve continuous planning movement.

findings.scenario: Unequal squads receive different bot backfill while viewers reconnect or switch submission channels.
findings.gap: One influence per viewer does not establish cohort fairness, stable eligibility, deduplication or defensive balancing.
findings.recommendation: Define identity and per-turn eligibility snapshots across channels; restore bounded cohort weighting and defensive balancing. Present weighting, K, denominator, bot voting and tie policies for human selection.

findings.scenario: Bot-generated danger increases bounty collected by human survivors.
findings.gap: JSON prohibits bots earning rewards but omits the stronger prohibition on bot-created farmable bounty; Markdown only implies human provenance.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly exclude bots and fixture events from human bounty creation and allocation, retaining immutable contribution provenance through recovery. Leave bounty amounts and reward splits for human choice.

findings.scenario: Repeated individually bounded obstructions combine into indefinite control denial or escalating damage.
findings.gap: No permanent control loss and no unavoidable death omit the original explicit bans on stun-lock and unbounded damage, including cumulative effects.
findings.recommendation: Restore both hard prohibitions and specify enforceable aggregate duration, placement, overlap and damage limits with a viable recovery path. Numeric balance values require selection before simulation.

findings.scenario: A timely chat message produces a model proposal after closure while the delivery deadline expires.
findings.gap: Phase durations do not define authoritative receipt versus completion cutoffs, deadline clock, suspension semantics or asynchronous processing.
findings.recommendation: Specify monotonic phase/match clocks, expiry ordering and pause policy. Require asynchronous bounded model work, local revalidation, explicit late rejection and no silent next-turn rollover; never wait for inference in the game loop.

findings.scenario: Provider failure occurs during reward commitment, followed by offline operation and live recovery.
findings.gap: An offline fixture alone does not specify continuity, ownership or duplicate-effect prevention.
findings.recommendation: Define canonical commands, deterministic time/seed, safe-boundary single-writer handover, durable accepted-command/reward records, uninterrupted rendering/simulation and health/state comparison before recovery. Keep fixture provenance visibly separate.

findings.scenario: A staged bullet-time sequence presents a replay as a live model decision.
findings.gap: The baseline omits the original three-minute demo target and actual sanitized message, recorded tool-call, measured latency, validation and execution evidence requirements.
findings.recommendation: Restore the demo evidence contract with persistent live/fixture/replay labels and distinct model, Codex and engine stages. Unmeasured timings or unexecuted integrations must remain explicitly illustrative.

findings.scenario: A character or attacker review agent is interpreted as an autonomous gameplay controller.
findings.gap: Rehearsal perspectives, human actors, avatar state and runtime AI services are conflated.
findings.recommendation: Create an authority table separating streamer navigation, viewer proposals, engine-owned character state, bounded red-team actions, operator controls and advisory AI. Do not infer autonomous character or attacker deployment from role critiques.

findings.scenario: A selected model or passing mock executor is reported as a working gameplay integration.
findings.gap: Routing documentation distinguishes selection from inference, but the product plan lacks an equivalent evidence boundary.
findings.recommendation: Carry task/provider/model/effort, policy and content hashes through a reusable injected-executor boundary. Preserve separate labels for selection, actual critique, mocked transport and observed gameplay; retain disabled providers, explicit budgets and no silent fallback.

findings.scenario: A valid data-only hotfix changes safety limits or replays an obsolete manifest.
findings.gap: Prohibiting executable hot-loading alone does not preserve game authority or establish trusted activation.
findings.recommendation: Specify approver authority, authenticated artifact/base/version binding, bounded DSL capabilities and atomic boundary activation. Revalidate hard safety invariants independently of model output; adopt the security review's anti-replay and recovery contracts.

findings.scenario: Passing PRODUCT's credential-free mock MVP criteria is presented as submission readiness.
findings.gap: Local fixture acceptance does not satisfy the actual Twitch connection and Codex evidence requirements recorded in hackathon research.
findings.recommendation: Separate offline-slice and submission gates. The latter needs evidenced Twitch operation, actual Codex work/session provenance and the required demo; obtain separate implementation/publication authorization. This does not require paid model inference.
